subject: BBME
title: Seminars in Biological and Biomedical Engineering
description: Mandatory attendance at the seminar series at which students present a seminar related to their research

restrictions.text: Only open to students registered in the second term or later of the M.Eng. in Biological and Biomedical Engineering (Thesis). Not open to students who have taken BMDE 600D1/2.

notes: 1. Students must register for both BBME 600D1 and BBME 600D2
2. Students must register for BBME 600D1 before registering for BBME 600D2
3. No credit will be given for this course unless both BBME 600D1 and BBME 600D2 are successfully completed in consecutive terms

subject: BBME
title: Internship 1
description: An internship/research project (minimum 360 hours) related to the practice of Biological and Biomedical Engineering supervised by a practitioner in the biological and biomedical engineering field within an industrial or institutional research centre environment.

restrictions.text: Only open to students registered in the M.Eng. in Biological and Biomedical Engineering; Non-Thesis program.

notes: Students will be supervised by a BBME faculty member and co-supervised by a qualified supervisor from the host organization.

subject: BBME
title: Internship 2
description: An internship/research project (minimum 360 hours) related to the practice of Biological and Biomedical Engineering supervised by a practitioner in the biological and biomedical engineering field within an industrial or institutional research centre environment.

restrictions.text: Only open to students registered in the M.Eng. in Biological and Biomedical Engineering; Non-Thesis program.

notes: This course may be completed in the same organization and under the same supervisor as BBME 681 to consolidate professional knowledge and experience, or in another institution to broaden professional experience and knowledge.
Students will be supervised by a BBME faculty member and co-supervised by a qualified supervisor from the host organization.

subject: BBME
title: PhD 1 Research in Biological and Biomedical Engineering 1
description: This course is part of a set of first-year research courses (Parts 1 and 2), meant for students who have been admitted directly from a bachelor’s program, that recognize the initial steps in research in the field of Biological and Biomedical Engineering. Students may begin developing their research project through literature reviews, research activities, and the exploration of initial research questions. They may become familiar with the relevant literature and ethical requirements of the field and, where appropriate, may begin preparing ethics review applications.
